youtube.title: A POLITICAL AGENDA
youtube.summary: Maree Buscke is joined by former Coromandel MP and Thames-Coromandel Mayor Sandra Goudie, and Sovereign leader Joshua Riley, to examine political influence, foreign lobbying, poorly drafted legislation, roadside drug testing, the India FTA and the growing debate over co-governance, rights and democracy ahead of the election. For more from Joshua Riley and Sovereign on X For election news that matters, get RCR Bites FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: JANET DICKSON
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan is joined by Janet Dickson following the cancellation of her real estate licence after she refused to complete the mandatory Te Kākano course. With the Government now changing the rules that led to her case, Janet explains why the fight is not over, what happens next and why she believes the issue affects professionals far beyond real estate. youtube.title: MEDIA MATTERS
youtube.summary: Maree and Marty examine growing concerns over Māori nationalism, identity politics and the effectiveness of Māori-focused government policies. They discuss Chris Trotter’s Haters and the Wreckers article, Willie Jackson’s Q+A interview with Jack Tame and whether targeted government spending has delivered better outcomes in education, health and crime. For more information: Q&A | Willie Jackson Interview Chris Trotter Article | The haters and the Wreckers

youtube.title: SONIA ELIJAH
youtube.summary: Paul Brennan talks with British investigative journalist Sonia Elijah about the BMJ's retraction of a paper documenting 3 million excess deaths across 47 countries, which she argues meets the hallmarks of scientific suppression rather than genuine research misconduct. For more information: Sonia's substack | Sonia Elijah Investigates Her article: BMJ Retracts 2024 Excess Deaths Paper for the Sin of Spreading “Misinformation” Her interview on RCR in May 2023 | Sonia Elijah on the Pfizer Safety Report for Pregnancy & Lactation For more on this | Jeffrey Tucker, Brownstone Institute Founder: What Fauci’s Diaries Reveal Stories you won’t see on the 6pm news — RCR Bites, delivered FREE every weekday.

youtube.title: WEEKLY ROUNDUP
youtube.summary: Dieuwe de Boer and William McGimpsey cover a busy week in immigration politics, starting with ACT's proposal to abolish permanent residency in New Zealand and require residents to spend real time in the country. They discuss Restore Britain's contested new paper on citizenship and national identity, Canadian police pressuring venues to cancel a migration conference, and Nathan Cofnas' push for a “hereditarian” rethink of racial disparities, before closing with Trump's sweeping US visa crackdowns.

youtube.title: RIDING SHOTGUN
youtube.summary: Rachel Stewart reflects on her own mortality and discovers that contemplating death can bring an unexpected sense of calm and perspective. She explores the Bhutanese practice of regularly thinking about death, her experience using the WeCroak app, and how reminders of mortality can help put everyday worries, anxieties and family dramas into perspective – sometimes with a much-needed dose of humour. Discover more from Rachel on Substack and X

youtube.title: There's no point in me coming to see you. Good luck.
youtube.summary: "There's no point in me coming to see you. Good luck." - Kathryn Pick, Former Principal quotes NZEI Union Representative After paying thousands in union fees, would you expect more than "good luck" from your union when vaccine mandates were causing a staffing crisis at your school? Maree Buscke speaks with former principal Kathryn Pick about being terminated during the 2021 vaccine mandates, the lack of support from ministries and unions, and the four-and-a-half-year investigation that ended in her being struck off the teaching register. 🎥 Watch here: https://rcr.media/episodes/kathryn-pick-former-principal-struck-off-for-standing-by-her-school-community #RCRMedia
